thread.title: iPhone 18 Pro: Upgrade Justified

author: priyanka.patel tech editor
title: iPhone 18 Pro: Upgrade Justified
text:
The iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max were released, sparking debate over whether their upgrades justify replacing recent models. While design and camera refinements offer tangible improvements, critics question if they’re enough to convince users to upgrade.
Early reviews highlight incremental improvements in hardware and camera capabilities, yet many users find the changes insufficient to justify replacing their iPhone 16 or 17 models. The iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max retain the familiar design of their predecessors, with subtle refinements. The Dynamic Island shrank slightly, freeing up screen real estate for more detailed Live Activities, according to TechRadar. The new Burgundy and Glacier color options, described as “lovely” and “shimmering,” also drew praise. However, the overall form factor and build quality closely mirror the iPhone 17 Pro, leading some reviewers to question if the changes are meaningful or merely cosmetic.
Will the iPhone 18 Pro give you a real
Storage remains a contentious issue. While the 18 Pro starts at 256GB—up from 128GB in the iPhone 16e—the base tier still feels inadequate for users who shoot 4K video regularly. The R30,000 price tag for the Pro model raises the question of why 512GB isn’t the standard base configuration. The iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max’s 48-megapixel main lens features a variable aperture, allowing users to adjust f-stop settings manually or automatically. This enhancement, TechRadar reported, should improve low-light performance and depth control. The Pro Controls interface, now fully customizable, gives photographers greater flexibility over shutter speed, aperture, and white balance.
The variable aperture is a first for Apple, but critics argue that the iPhone 17 Pro already delivered excellent low-light performance. The new Photographic Styles and AI-infused editing features, IOL noted, feel more like software refinements than hardware breakthroughs. For casual users, the differences may be negligible. The 48-megapixel main lens is paired with a 48-megapixel telephoto lens and a 48-megapixel ultra-wide lens, enabling zoom capabilities from 0.5x to 8x optical and up to 40x digitally. The Dynamic Island’s smaller size allows it to show up to three Live Activities at once, with each displaying more detail. For instance, if you have music playing and a timer next to it, the time left is now visible.
The A20 Pro chip, Apple’s fastest yet, promises a 40% boost in GPU performance and improved thermal management. TechRadar observed that the chip’s “Super Cores” deliver smooth performance, but the lack of a dramatic visual or functional shift left some reviewers underwhelmed. The larger vapor chamber and redesigned thermal architecture are expected to keep the device cooler during heavy use, though this remains untested in real-world scenarios. Apple claims the iPhone 18 Pro offers longer battery life, but early hands-on experiences IOL suggest this is the one area where the improvements are hardest to quantify. Without extended testing, it’s unclear if the new battery life is a game-changer or merely a marginal gain.
I just tried the iPhone 18 Pro
The iPhone 18 Pro’s upgrades reflect Apple’s strategy of refining existing features rather than introducing radical changes. While the variable aperture, A20 chip, and new color options are notable, they fall short of the “must-have” status that previous flagship models have achieved. For users invested in the iPhone ecosystem, the improvements may justify an upgrade. However, for those with a 16 or 17 model, the benefits are less clear. The iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max do still pack the Pro-grade camera system, but the lack of a dramatic shift in design or functionality leaves some questioning the necessity of the upgrade.
The hands-on experience with the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max took place after Apple’s Surprise and Shine event. TechRadar’s review noted the new variable aperture lens’s visible opening and closing, a feature that allows users to adjust light intake for better low-light photography. The device runs iOS 27, which TechRadar described as “really smooth.” The new thermal architecture, including the larger vapor chamber, is designed to mitigate heat, particularly around the raised camera plateau. Despite these advancements, the overall sentiment remains mixed, with many critics leaning toward recommending patience for future iterations.
For users who prioritize camera innovation, the variable aperture and Pro Controls represent significant strides. However, for the average user, the differences may not justify the cost. The iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max’s value proposition hinges on whether users prioritize incremental improvements or demand transformative changes. With the Pro Max’s R30,000 price tag and the continued dominance of the iPhone 17 Pro’s capabilities, the upgrade debate is far from settled.

TechRadar observed that the chip’s “Super Cores” deliver smooth performance, but the lack of a dramatic visual or functional shift left some reviewers underwhelmed. Apple claims the iPhone 18 Pro offers longer battery life, but early hands-on experiences IOL suggest this is the one area where the improvements are hardest to quantify.
